entities.summary: The Iskender Bey Mosque is a former mosque in the town of Giannitsa, in Central Macedonia, in northern Greece. The mosque was built in the early 16th century, during the Ottoman era, by İskender Bey Evrenosoğlu, after whom it was named, who was the grandson of Gazi Evrenos, the founder of Giannitsa. The mosque was abandoned during the 1910s, and it is in partial ruins, in need of restoration. It is not accessible to the public. It is one of the three surviving Ottoman mosques in Giannitsa.
